## Overview

The NIXL pull connector rejects a GQA model whose prefill TP exceeds its KV-head count when decode TP is smaller (for example, Llama-3.3-70B with 8 KV heads at P TP16 → D TP4). This PR supports that case: D reads one P replica per KV head and notifies the replicas it skips.

## Claims

- P_TP > num_kv_heads with P_TP > D_TP now handshakes and serves in pull mode, for non-MLA, non-Mamba models. Before this change, every request failed at the `assert not (tp_ratio < 0 and is_kv_replicated)` handshake check.
- Skipped replica ranks get the read-done notification, so they free their blocks at once instead of holding them until the KV lease expires.
- No behavior change for other topologies: MLA, Mamba, push mode, and non-replicated or P_TP <= D_TP setups take the same paths as before.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k gqa_replicated`):
- `test_handshake_gqa_replicated_p_gt_d[4-16-8]` / `[1-8-4]` check that the handshake validates, plus one replica per head and rejection of a wrong `block_len`.
- `test_gqa_replicated_pull_round_trip[8-4-1-0]` / `[8-4-2-1]` / `[16-8-4-2]` (P TP, KV heads, D TP, D rank) run the real `register_kv_caches` → handshake → `start_load_kv` path on CPU tensors. An in-process NIXL stand-in copies the bytes of every descriptor and routes notifications. Each test checks two things:
  - The whole decode cache matches the expected image: each head slot of the request's blocks holds the first prefill replica of that head, and nothing else changes.
  - Every handshaked prefill rank, read or skipped, frees the request.

Base (origin/main):
```
E           AssertionError
FAILED ...::TestNixlHandshake::test_handshake_gqa_replicated_p_gt_d[4-16-8]
FAILED ...::TestNixlHandshake::test_handshake_gqa_replicated_p_gt_d[1-8-4]
FAILED ...::test_gqa_replicated_pull_round_trip[8-4-1-0]
FAILED ...::test_gqa_replicated_pull_round_trip[8-4-2-1]
FAILED ...::test_gqa_replicated_pull_round_trip[16-8-4-2]
5 failed, 1 passed, 196 deselected
```
The round-trip test also fails in two other cases:
- With the skipped-replica notification reverted: `AssertionError: P rank 1` (P rank 1 never frees the request).
- With the head-slot offset reversed: `AssertionError: layer 0`.

With this PR:
```
6 passed, 196 deselected
```
The same 6 tests pass on a B200 host with NIXL 1.5.0 installed.

The rest of `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` passes locally: `test_tp_mapping`, `test_nixl_connector`, `test_nixl_push_connector`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry`, `test_nixl_connector_hma`. Three tests need Ray or a real NIXL install, and they fail the same way on main in this environment: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]`, `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[None]`, and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]`.

**End to end on this branch**:
- Setup: 1× B200 host (8 GPUs), NIXL 1.5.0 LIBFABRIC, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC`.
- Model: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, 2 KV heads, so P TP4 holds each head on 2 ranks. P TP4 on GPUs 4-7, D on GPUs 0-1.
- Load: 8K input / 128 output.
- Reference: a single engine at the D TP, on the remaining GPUs.

| P TP → D TP | block | origin/main | c64 req/s | KV xfer avg | expired P leases | exact vs D-TP mono (TP4 mono vs D-TP mono) | gsm8k flexible (D-TP mono) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 → 1 | 32 | handshake assert, HTTP 500 | 33.3 | 134 ms | 0 | 12/21 (11/21) | 0.632 (0.634) |
| 4 → 1 | 128 | | 41.8 | 9 ms | 0 | 12/21 | 0.632 |
| 4 → 2 | 32 | handshake assert, HTTP 500 | 42.4 | 8 ms | 0 | 16/21 (16/21) | 0.631 (0.632) |
| 4 → 2 | 128 | | 41.2 | 5 ms | 0 | 16/21 | 0.633 |

- Every run had 0 failed transfers, 0 notifications after expiry, and 256/256 requests completed.
- The exact-match column compares 21 prompts × 48 greedy tokens against the reference. The value in parentheses is the same comparison between two single engines, TP4 and the D TP. That is the normal cross-TP numerics level.
- gsm8k: lm-eval `local-completions`, 5-shot, flexible-extract. The model's strict-match score is about 0.10 in every configuration, single engine included.

Larger model, same change backported to v0.29.0 (not run on this branch): Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (8 KV heads) with P TP16 → D TP4.
- Before the change: handshake assert, 0 requests completed.
- With the backport: 3.5 req/s (best, block 32), 120 ms KV transfer, 0 expired P leases, 18/21 exact vs D-TP mono.
- The prefill engine was not CUDA; decode was B200 TP4.

## Details

**Root cause.**
1. `compute_tp_mapping` already deduplicates replicated GQA heads with `np.unique`: a D rank reads exactly one P rank per KV head it owns.
2. The block_len check already uses per-rank head counts (#45330).
3. `_validate_remote_agent_handshake` still asserted the whole case away, and nothing notified the replicas that are never read.

**Flow (P TP8, 4 KV heads, D TP1):**
1. P ranks {0,1}, {2,3}, {4,5}, {6,7} each hold the same head.
2. D handshakes with all 8 P ranks, as `handshake_target_ranks` already does.
3. The mapping picks source ranks 0, 2, 4, 6, and D posts four head-sliced READs into its local head slots.
4. D sends `"<p_req_id>:<local_consumers>"` to ranks 1, 3, 5, 7. Every P rank then reaches its expected notification count and frees the request's blocks.

**Changes:**
- `_is_gqa_replicated_pull()` detects the case (pull mode, `tp_ratio < 0`, not MLA, not Mamba, `is_kv_replicated`).
- The handshake no longer asserts on it, and validates the remote `block_len` as head-split rather than replicated.
- The layout check requires block-contiguous heads, the same as other head-split transfers.
- The existing MLA "notify the unread ranks" path is generalized from "every rank except the single one read" to "every handshaked rank not read". For MLA the behavior is identical.

**Limitations:**
- Push mode is unchanged and still rejects a remote TP above both the local TP and num_kv_heads. P validates D there, and D can validate P through its heartbeat handshake when P has PP=1. In that case D logs a failed handshake, and the registration handshake then connects it (this already happens on main). Push with P_TP > num_kv_heads > D_TP has not been validated end to end.
- Throughput for P_TP > D_TP is governed by the head-sliced descriptor size, the same as non-replicated heterogeneous TP. A larger `--block-size` helps a lot. Example: B200 TP4 → TP1 at 8K went from 3.2 to 18.1 req/s when the block size changed from 32 to 128.

**Side note.** `test_mla_broadcast_notif_uses_remote_request_id` is indented inside the preceding module-level test function, so pytest never collects it. This PR leaves it untouched. The new module-level test covers the shared notify path.

Agreed that after this change it can only fire in push mode. One correction: P isn't the only side that validates there. D's heartbeat handshake is a full handshake when P has PP=1 (`_send_heartbeats` → `_ensure_handshake(..., notif_agents_only=False)`). It can be the first contact: heartbeats are scheduled from `on_new_request`, but the PUSH_REG is only staged after block allocation, so a request still waiting on D sends a heartbeat first. So the assert also fires on D for P_TP > num_kv_heads > D_TP.

I checked with real push scheduler and worker objects over the ZMQ handshake listener (P TP8 with 4 KV heads, D TP1). D logs `handshake_setup_failed`, then the notif-only PUSH_REG handshake connects it, and the registration reaches every P rank. main behaves the same, with an empty `AssertionError()`. I can add that test to `test_nixl_push_connector.py` if useful.

In c970e63087 the message no longer names a side: `NIXL push mode does not support a remote TP (8) above both the local TP (1) and num_kv_heads (4); use pull mode.` I updated the comment and the Limitations in the description to match.

- Every run had 0 failed transfers, 0 notifications after expiry, and 256/256 requests completed.
- The exact-match column compares 21 prompts × 48 greedy tokens against the reference. The value in parentheses is the same comparison between two single engines, TP4 and the D TP. That is the normal cross-TP numerics level.
- gsm8k: lm-eval `local-completions`, 5-shot, flexible-extract. The model's strict-match score is about 0.10 in every configuration, single engine included.

Larger model, same change backported to v0.29.0 (not run on this branch): Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (8 KV heads) with P TP16 → D TP4.
- Before the change: handshake assert, 0 requests completed.
- With the backport: 3.5 req/s (best, block 32), 120 ms KV transfer, 0 expired P leases, 18/21 exact vs D-TP mono.
- The prefill engine was not CUDA; decode was B200 TP4.

## Details

**Root cause.**
1. `compute_tp_mapping` already deduplicates replicated GQA heads with `np.unique`: a D rank reads exactly one P rank per KV head it owns.
2. The block_len check already uses per-rank head counts (#45330).
3. `_validate_remote_agent_handshake` still asserted the whole case away, and nothing notified the replicas that are never read.

**Flow (P TP8, 4 KV heads, D TP1):**
1. P ranks {0,1}, {2,3}, {4,5}, {6,7} each hold the same head.
2. D handshakes with all 8 P ranks, as `handshake_target_ranks` already does.
3. The mapping picks source ranks 0, 2, 4, 6, and D posts four head-sliced READs into its local head slots.
4. D sends `"<p_req_id>:<local_consumers>"` to ranks 1, 3, 5, 7. Every P rank then reaches its expected notification count and frees the request's blocks.

**Changes:**
- `_is_gqa_replicated_pull()` detects the case (pull mode, `tp_ratio < 0`, not MLA, not Mamba, `is_kv_replicated`).
- The handshake no longer asserts on it, and validates the remote `block_len` as head-split rather than replicated.
- The layout check requires block-contiguous heads, the same as other head-split transfers.
- The existing MLA "notify the unread ranks" path is generalized from "every rank except the single one read" to "every handshaked rank not read". For MLA the behavior is identical.

**Limitations:**
- Push mode is unchanged and still rejects a remote TP above both the local TP and num_kv_heads. P validates D there, and D can validate P through its heartbeat handshake when P has PP=1. In that case D logs a failed handshake, and the registration handshake then connects it (this already happens on main). Push with P_TP > num_kv_heads > D_TP has not been validated end to end.
- Throughput for P_TP > D_TP is governed by the head-sliced descriptor size, the same as non-replicated heterogeneous TP. A larger `--block-size` helps a lot. Example: B200 TP4 → TP1 at 8K went from 3.2 to 18.1 req/s when the block size changed from 32 to 128.

**Side note.** `test_mla_broadcast_notif_uses_remote_request_id` is indented inside the preceding module-level test function, so pytest never collects it. This PR leaves it untouched. The new module-level test covers the shared notify path.

Agreed that after this change it can only fire in push mode. One correction: P isn't the only side that validates there. D's heartbeat handshake is a full handshake when P has PP=1 (`_send_heartbeats` → `_ensure_handshake(..., notif_agents_only=False)`). It can be the first contact: heartbeats are scheduled from `on_new_request`, but the PUSH_REG is only staged after block allocation, so a request still waiting on D sends a heartbeat first. So the assert also fires on D for P_TP > num_kv_heads > D_TP.

I checked with real push scheduler and worker objects over the ZMQ handshake listener (P TP8 with 4 KV heads, D TP1). D logs `handshake_setup_failed`, then the notif-only PUSH_REG handshake connects it, and the registration reaches every P rank. main behaves the same, with an empty `AssertionError()`. I can add that test to `test_nixl_push_connector.py` if useful.

In c970e63087 the message no longer names a side: `NIXL push mode does not support a remote TP (8) above both the local TP (1) and num_kv_heads (4); use pull mode.` I updated the comment and the Limitations in the description to match.
